key_insight: Multimodal LLMs often answer table-based questions correctly but frequently fail to reliably cite the exact rows and columns that support their answers; attribution fidelity varies strongly by table format and prompting strategy.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of systematic evaluation for structured-data attribution — i.e., whether mLLMs can point to the specific table cells (rows/columns) that justify their answers across Markdown, JSON and image-based tables.
method: Assemble ViTaB-A: an evaluation suite of questions over tables in multiple formats (Markdown, JSON, images) with ground-truth row/column annotations.
Run several state-of-the-art mLLMs under diverse prompting strategies and measure both answer accuracy and attribution/localization fidelity using per-cell/row/column metrics.
Analyze how table format and prompt design affect attribution quality and report common failure modes and patterns.
impact: Provides a practical benchmark and diagnostic insights so practitioners can choose models and prompts that not only answer correctly but also transparently cite supporting table data—improving trust, interpretability, and compliance for applications using structured inputs.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing dataset (multiple table formats) → mLLMs → answer + citation evaluation metrics

Side-by-side example table image with highlighted true supporting cells vs. model-cited cells (correct/incorrect)
Bar chart showing effect of different prompting strategies on attribution vs. answer accuracy
paper_title: ViTaB-A: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models on Visual Table Attribution
paper_authors: Yahia Alqurnawi, Preetom Biswas, Anmol Rao, Tejas Anvekar, Chitta Baral
